_note: Fixture corpus for the retrieval evaluation (PLAN.md 3.7). Companies, filings and statements are invented for testing; they are not real filings or real central-bank text.

filings.text: Our anvil business depends on a single steel supplier in Ohio; an interruption at that mill could halt production for up to twelve weeks.
Net sales rose 14 percent to 2.1 billion dollars, driven by rocket-skate volumes, while gross margin narrowed to 31 percent on freight costs.
We ended the year with 640 million dollars of cash and an undrawn 500 million dollar revolving credit facility maturing in 2028.
A product liability class action concerning the portable hole product line is pending in the District of Arizona; we believe the claims lack merit.
Lithium carbonate prices drive most of our battery cell cost, and a 20 percent price increase would reduce operating margin by about three points.
Electric scooter deliveries reached 410 thousand units; average selling price fell 6 percent as we cut prices in Europe to defend share.
Free cash flow was negative 220 million dollars; we raised 750 million dollars of convertible notes due 2029 at a 2.5 percent coupon.
The national highway safety regulator opened a preliminary evaluation into brake failures on the model S3 scooter after 37 complaints.
Our semiconductor test equipment orders are concentrated: three foundry customers accounted for 58 percent of revenue, and export controls limit shipments to China.
Backlog grew to 3.4 billion dollars and book-to-bill was 1.3, led by advanced packaging probe cards.
The board authorised a 1 billion dollar share repurchase programme and raised the quarterly dividend to 0.45 dollars per share.
A competitor filed a patent infringement suit in the Eastern District of Texas alleging our thermal chuck design copies its wafer cooling patents.
Our regional hospitals rely on Medicaid reimbursement for 41 percent of patient revenue, so state budget cuts directly reduce our earnings.
Same-facility admissions increased 3.2 percent, and contract nurse labor expense fell by 90 million dollars as staffing stabilised.
Net leverage was 4.8 times EBITDA; we intend to sell two rural hospitals in Kansas to bring leverage below 4.0 times by 2026.
The Department of Justice issued a civil investigative demand regarding our billing for emergency department observation stays.
Advertising revenue on our podcast network is cyclical, and a pullback by direct-to-consumer brands reduced CPMs in the first quarter.
Monthly active listeners reached 96 million and subscription revenue grew 27 percent after the launch of the ad-free tier.
We repaid the 300 million dollar term loan early using proceeds from the sale of our live events division.
Music publishers sued us for copyright infringement over background tracks used in archived episodes, seeking statutory damages.
Our offshore wind turbine installations face weather delays in the North Sea, and vessel availability constrains the construction schedule.
We recorded a 1.2 billion dollar impairment on the cancelled Atlantic Shores project after offtake prices failed to cover higher interest costs.
Investment tax credits transferable under the clean energy law provided 400 million dollars of liquidity, and we suspended the dividend.
Fishing associations challenged our federal permit for the Gull Bank array, arguing the environmental review ignored cumulative effects on scallop grounds.

statements.title: FOMC statement (fixture) September 2024
statements.text: The Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by one half percentage point to 4.75 to 5 percent, having gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.

statements.title: FOMC statement (fixture) December 2024
statements.text: The Committee lowered the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 4.25 to 4.5 percent and will consider the extent and timing of additional adjustments carefully.

statements.title: FOMC statement (fixture) March 2025
statements.text: The Committee held the federal funds rate steady and decided to slow the pace of decline of its securities holdings by reducing the monthly Treasury redemption cap to 5 billion dollars.

statements.title: ECB monetary policy decision (fixture) June 2024
statements.text: The Governing Council decided to reduce the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points, cutting the deposit facility rate to 3.75 percent after nine months of holding steady.

statements.title: ECB monetary policy decision (fixture) October 2024
statements.text: The deposit facility rate was lowered to 3.25 percent as incoming information showed the disinflationary process is well on track and euro area growth surprised to the downside.

statements.title: ECB monetary policy decision (fixture) June 2025
statements.text: The Governing Council lowered the deposit facility rate to 2 percent and judged that euro area headline inflation is now at around its 2 percent medium-term target.

statements.title: Bank of England Monetary Policy Summary (fixture) August 2024
statements.text: The Monetary Policy Committee voted by a majority of 5 to 4 to reduce Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points to 5 percent, the first cut since 2020.

statements.title: Bank of England Monetary Policy Summary (fixture) February 2025
statements.text: Bank Rate was cut to 4.5 percent; the Committee noted that UK GDP growth had weakened and that services price inflation remained sticky above 5 percent.

statements.title: Bank of Japan statement on monetary policy (fixture) March 2024
statements.text: The Bank of Japan ended negative interest rates, setting the uncollateralised overnight call rate at around 0 to 0.1 percent, and abolished yield curve control on Japanese government bonds.

statements.title: Bank of Japan statement on monetary policy (fixture) January 2025
statements.text: The Policy Board raised the short-term policy rate to around 0.5 percent, citing firm spring wage negotiations and the yen's weakness pushing up import prices.
